# FLAGSHIP ROOFING DEMO SITE — BUILD DOSSIER

**For content writers. This document is the single source of truth. Raw research and verification results are synthesized here. Where the Verify phase corrected a claim, it is marked [VERIFIED]. Every number carries its source.**

---

## SECTION 1: PER-BRAND FACT SHEETS

---

### 1A. GAF

#### Certification Tier

**Exact defensible phrasing:** "One of fewer than 2% of roofing contractors in North America to earn GAF Master Elite® status."

[VERIFIED] GAF's own pages use "only about 2% of roofers in North America are GAF Master Elite® Contractors" and "less than 2%." The phrase "top 2%" does not appear verbatim on gaf.com — do not use it. The geographic qualifier "North America" (not "US") is GAF's own framing; they operate in Canada too.

**Requirements to earn Master Elite:**
- Valid state/provincial roofing license
- Minimum $1 million general liability + workers' compensation coverage
- 7+ years in business
- Satisfactory BBB rating and community reputation
- Completion of GAF-administered training and annual testing
- Ongoing installation volume thresholds to maintain status
- Credit rating check; GAF controls admission — not open to all applicants

GAF Master Elite is invitation-controlled, not self-applied.

Do NOT conflate "Master Elite" with "GAF President's Club" — President's Club is an annual performance award within Master Elite, requires annual re-qualification, and is not a permanent designation.

#### Warranty Terms

**Golden Pledge (Master Elite exclusive — cannot be offered by any lower tier):**
- Material coverage: 50-year non-prorated (Lifetime on shingles) [VERIFIED]
- Workmanship coverage: 25 years for standard GAF Lifetime shingles [VERIFIED]
- Workmanship coverage: 30 years for Timberline UHDZ on single-family residences [VERIFIED — use 30 years; one secondary source cited 40 years but this is NOT consistently corroborated; do not use 40 years]
- No dollar limit on covered claims
- Includes tear-off and disposal for covered failures
- Requires one GAF shingle + one product from each of five accessory categories: (1) Leak Barrier, (2) Roof Deck Protection, (3) Starter Strip Shingles, (4) Attic Ventilation, (5) Hip & Ridge Cap Shingles
- Transferable once: transferred within first 20 years = new owner receives full remaining coverage; transferred after 20 years = coverage reduces to a 2-year prorated period. Do not write "transfers in full at any time" — inaccurate for older homes.

**Silver Pledge (available to GAF Certified Plus or Master Elite — NOT basic Certified tier alone):**
- Workmanship coverage: 10 years
- Material coverage: 50-year non-prorated (architectural shingles); 25-year (3-tab)

**System Plus (minimum GAF Certified contractor):**
- Workmanship coverage from GAF: 0 years (materials only; contractor may separately provide ~2 years)
- Material coverage: 50-year non-prorated (architectural); 20-year (3-tab)

**WindProven Limited Wind Warranty:**
- Industry-first: no maximum wind speed limitation [VERIFIED]
- Term: 15 years
- Requires LayerLock-labeled shingles + four qualifying GAF accessories: Starter Strip Shingles, Roof Deck Protection, Ridge Cap Shingles, and either a Leak Barrier OR Attic Ventilation product
- Covers shingles only — does NOT extend to accessory products
- Do not write copy implying the entire roof system is covered under WindProven

#### Product Lines + Key Specs

**Timberline HDZ:**
- GAF's #1-selling shingle; best-selling shingle in North America
- LayerLock technology: nails pass through two shingle courses, asphalt-to-asphalt bond cures into monolithic holding layer
- Qualifies for WindProven unlimited wind warranty
- 25-year StainGuard Plus algae warranty
- Golden Pledge workmanship: 25 years

**Timberline UHDZ:**
- 10% more Time-Release Algae-Fighting Technology vs HDZ
- 30-year StainGuard Plus Pro algae warranty (vs 25-year on HDZ)
- Golden Pledge workmanship: 30 years (single-family)
- Also qualifies for WindProven unlimited wind warranty

**Grand Sequoia:**
- Dimensions: 17" x 40" (oversized format)
- Weight: up to 50% heavier than standard architectural shingles
- Appearance: mimics hand-split cedar shake
- Standard wind rating: 130 mph (with GAF Starter Strip Shingles and proper nailing)
- Grand Sequoia AS variant: UL 2218 Class 4 impact resistance (highest possible) — Class 4 applies to the AS variant ONLY, not standard Grand Sequoia or Grand Sequoia RS
- LayerLock-equipped; eligible for WindProven unlimited wind warranty
- Class A fire resistance (UL)

#### 3 Copy Angles

1. "Fewer than 2% of roofing contractors in North America ever earn GAF Master Elite status — when you hire us, you're hiring the top tier, not the average contractor." (Source: GAF.com)

2. "GAF backs our work for 25 years — not just the shingles. The Golden Pledge warranty covers labor AND materials, because the majority of roof leaks come from installation mistakes, not the shingles themselves." [Note: the "80% from installation errors" figure is widely repeated in GAF contractor marketing but its primary research source is not cited in any fetched document — use as a sales claim with that context; do not present as verified statistic if a client asks for sourcing]

3. "WindProven: an industry first — the only roofing wind warranty with no maximum wind speed. Timberline HDZ with LayerLock technology means your roof is engineered to hold, not just rated to hold."

**Exact defensible phrasing:** "Among less than 1% of roofing contractors nationwide recognized as Owens Corning Platinum Preferred — an invitation-only designation." [VERIFIED]

[VERIFIED] OC's official roofing rewards page (roofing.owenscorning.com/roofing/rewards-program) states verbatim: "Platinum Preferred Contractors represent less than 1% of the industry and are the only contractors who can offer the Platinum Protection Roofing System Limited Warranty." **Preferred Contractor (middle):** Basic certification, licensing, insurance, training. Can offer Preferred Protection warranty — NOT Platinum Protection.

**Platinum Protection Limited Warranty (Platinum Preferred exclusive):**
- Workmanship coverage: 25 years non-prorated, backed directly by Owens Corning — not just the local contractor. If contractor goes out of business, OC still honors it. This is a key differentiator.

**TruDefinition Duration (standard):**
- SureNail Technology: woven-fabric strip embedded in the nailing zone, creating triple-layer reinforcement and nailing target 10x wider than a standard nail line

**Duration FLEX:**

- Wind warranty: 130 mph
- 10-year algae resistance warranty (do not blanket-claim all Duration shingles carry same algae warranty — varies by SKU)

**Duration STORM:**
- Impact class: Class 4 via patented WeatherGuard Technology (NOT SBS modified asphalt — do not conflate with FLEX)

**TruDefinition color technology:** multi-granule colors + deliberate shadowing for dimensional color contrast visible from street.

2025 Color of the Year: "Merlot" (TruDefinition Duration Designer)
2026 Color of the Year: "Evergreen Mist" (TruDefinition Duration Designer, available January 1, 2026)

OC — Women's Choice Award: 8 consecutive years as the roofing brand women would most recommend to family and friends.

2. "Less than 1% of US roofing contractors earn Platinum Preferred status. It's not self-declared — it's invitation-only, screened by Owens Corning on licensing, insurance, installation quality, and financial stability." (Source: OC official rewards program page)

#### Certification Tier

**Tier structure:**

**NEX Polymer Modified (Rubberized) Asphalt — proprietary technology across Vista and Legacy lines:**
- 30% greater strength vs industry standard
- 65% greater granule adhesion vs industry standard

**Smog-reducing granules (3M-supplied photocatalytic coating):**
- Converts nitrogen oxides (NOx) into water-soluble nitrates washed away by rain

### Cost Drivers (use as content blocks explaining price variation)

1. **Roof footprint vs. living area:** Single-story homes have nearly twice the roof footprint of two-story homes with the same square footage — larger roof = higher cost.
2. **Pitch premium:** Steep slopes (8/12–12/12) add 30–50% to labor cost. Safety equipment, slower installation speed, and higher workers' comp exposure drive this.
3. **Tear-off layers:** $0.40–$2.00/sq ft per layer. Each additional layer beyond one increases labor and dump fees.
4. **Decking/sheathing damage:** $2–$5/sq ft or $75–$120/sheet for damaged/rotted areas. Cannot be assessed until after tear-off — always disclose as a hidden-cost risk.
5. **Chimney flashing:** $500–$2,000 add-on.
6. **Skylights:** $300–$600 per skylight to reframe and flash.
7. **Valley repairs:** $400–$1,000+.
8. **Dormers and complex rooflines:** Add 10–20% to labor.
9. **Material choice:** The largest single variable in the project price.
10. **Contractor tier/warranty tier:** Golden Pledge or Platinum Protection requires the full accessory system — more material line items = higher total.

### Financing Presentation Rules

**LEGAL — TILA/Regulation Z compliance (mandatory):**

Any webpage or ad that advertises a specific monthly payment, a promotional period, a low APR, or "same as cash" MUST disclose the corresponding APR in equal or greater prominence. This is FTC-enforced.

Safe pattern: "As low as $X/month with approved credit — representative example: $12,000 financed over 60 months at 9.99% APR = $254.95/month."

**GreenSky deferred-interest — CRITICAL LEGAL NOTE:**

GreenSky promotional plans are NOT "0% interest" or "interest-free." Interest accrues monthly during the promo period; it is only forgiven if the balance is paid in full before expiry. Post-promo APR: 15.85%–24.99%.

BANNED copy: "0% interest," "interest-free," "free financing"

REQUIRED copy: "No interest if paid in full within [X] months" — with explicit disclosure that interest accrues and is back-charged if balance is not paid in full.

**Enrollment requirement:** Do not name a specific lender's product on the website unless the contractor is an active enrolled dealer of that program. Generic framing is safer if enrollment is uncertain: "flexible financing available — ask about promotional payment options."

**General monthly-payment framing example (safe):** "A $12,000 roof replacement financed over 60 months at 8.99% APR is approximately $249/month — less than most car payments, and protecting the largest asset you own."

## SECTION 3: STORM/INSURANCE CONTENT PACK

---

### Hail Damage Sign List

Signs visible to a trained inspector (many invisible from ground):

1. **Granule loss with exposed black substrate/mat** — shiny appearance where granule bond has fractured
2. **Soft circular depressions (bruising)** — dark-colored, random distribution across the deck; feels soft when pressed, described as "bruising like an apple"; caused by fractures in the fiberglass mat beneath the asphalt layer
3. **Random (non-directional) pattern** — hail marks have no directional alignment across the roof
4. **Dents on soft metals** — gutters, downspouts, flashing, chimney caps, AC fins, vent covers. Fresh impact craters on aluminum and copper reveal exact hailstone diameter to adjusters; spatter marks (clean spots where hail removed oxidation/dirt) are adjuster-recognized evidence
5. **Fractured granule bonds** — internal damage not visible as a depression but reduces future weather resistance. 2025 peer-reviewed study (Frontiers in Materials) confirms sub-severe hailstones under 1 inch in diameter can significantly reduce shingle resistance to future hail and accelerate aging [VERIFIED — high-confidence primary research source]
6. **Cracking or splitting of older shingles** — IBHS 2025 research found conventional asphalt shingle performance degrades significantly with age when hit by wind-driven hail [VERIFIED]

"Soft metals don't lie" is a verified, adjuster-accepted evidence standard — lead with this on inspection pages.

---

### Wind Damage Sign List

Signs (directional pattern — distinguishes from hail):

1. **Lifted or curled shingle edges** — factory-applied adhesive seal strip has failed; typically occurs on the windward face
2. **Horizontal creases running across shingle tabs** — caused by wind lifting and repeatedly flexing the shingle
3. **Missing shingles** — the most obvious sign; exposes underlying decking and felt
4. **Exposed roofing nails** — shingles blown or lifted off, leaving nails visible
5. **Directional pattern** — unlike random hail distribution, wind damage traces the prevailing wind direction

---

### Claim Process Steps (roofer-assists perspective)

These are the steps a roofing contractor legitimately assists with — stay within these lanes. See Legal Guardrails section below for what is prohibited.

1. **Contractor pre-inspection:** independent inspection and photo documentation before homeowner files — establishes baseline damage evidence
2. **Homeowner files claim:** homeowner contacts insurer; contractor does NOT file on their behalf
3. **Contractor attends adjuster inspection:** legitimate role — provides independent technical scope, ensures covered items are not missed; does NOT negotiate settlement
4. **Insurer issues scope of loss:** the official damage assessment from the carrier
5. **Contractor reviews scope, submits supplement if needed:** if covered items were missed, contractor formally documents and requests supplement — this is a legitimate process, not bid inflation
6. **Agreed scope triggers build phase:** once scope is settled between homeowner and insurer, the build begins

## SECTION 4: CITY-PAGE DIFFERENTIATION PLAYBOOK

---

### Required Local Elements (every city page must have all of these)

These are the elements that distinguish a city page from a penalized "doorway page" under Google's March 2024 spam policy. The policy explicitly defines scaled content abuse as "many pages generated for the primary purpose of manipulating Search rankings" and gives the example of "spinning out cookie cutter pages that differ only in city names." [VERIFIED — confirmed on Google's own March 2024 spam policy documentation]

1. **Hyper-local job count or portfolio reference:** "We've replaced X+ roofs in [City] since [year]" — a first-party statistic that cannot be fabricated by a clone. This is the single most defensible proof of genuine local presence.

2. **City/county permit jurisdiction callout:** Name the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and specific requirement. Example: "The [City] Building Department requires a permit for any roof replacement exceeding 100 sq ft, with a final inspection before occupancy." In 16 US states, building code adoption occurs at the local level — permit content is genuinely city-unique. Estimate differences attributable to local code variation can exceed 25%. Do not fabricate permit details — verify the actual AHJ and current code version for each city.

3. **Weather exposure narrative specific to that city:** Do not write "we serve [city]" — describe the meteorological threat. Examples by climate type: Gulf Coast = wind-driven rain + salt-air accelerating granule loss; Mountain foothills = freeze-thaw cycling causing flashing separation; NC Piedmont = spring hail season + summer high-heat cycling. Source to NOAA or local weather history data.

4. **Housing era / architecture angle:** Each US city has a dominant construction era. Example: 1940s–1960s city = predominantly hip-roof brick ranchers on 3-tab shingles; 1980s–1990s suburb = dimensional shingles on steep-slope colonials. Name the era and the specific failure modes associated with it. No other city's page can share this content.

5. **Local material recommendation:** Name the locally optimal product and why (e.g., Class 4 impact shingles for hail-belt NC cities, metal roofing in fire-risk western areas, algae-resistant shingles in humid Southeast markets). HOA rules and local code may restrict cedar shake (common in fire-prone western cities).

6. **Neighborhood-anchored trust signals:** Name 3–5 recognizable neighborhoods or subdivisions the crew has worked in. Readers immediately confirm the roofer knows the area — a token-swap clone cannot replicate this.

7. **City-specific FAQ block:** Source FAQ questions from Google's "People Also Ask" for "[city] roofing" searches — they genuinely vary by city (coastal cities ask about hurricane insurance; Midwest cities ask about hail claims; mountain cities ask about snow loads). This differentiates the FAQ organically.

8. **City-specific reviews with provenance:** Attribute reviews to neighborhood or subdivision ("— Mike T., Lakewood Hills resident"). Schema markup the review with the local address region. This is Sterling Sky's documented approach to scaling genuine content across 35+ pages.

9. **Community presence proof:** Name the specific [City] Chamber of Commerce membership, local charity sponsorships, youth sports team sponsorships, or local news/media appearances. This is the "company connection to area" signal Sterling Sky identifies as a trust differentiator. Generates reciprocal local backlink potential from complementary businesses.

10. **Local landmark references:** Tie the service description to recognizable local landmarks, parks, lakes, popular neighborhoods, or city nicknames. "We service homes from [Neighborhood A] to [Landmark B]" creates a geographic specificity no clone can mimic.

---

### Structural Variation Techniques

Vary section ORDER across city pages — not just content. This structural divergence is a documented quality signal (Sang Froid Web Design research) and makes pages feel editorially distinct even when service descriptions share boilerplate.

Rotation examples:
- City A: Weather data block → Job portfolio gallery → Service description → Permit/code explainer → Reviews → CTA
- City B: Reviews → Job portfolio gallery → Weather data block → Service description → Community presence → CTA
- City C: Permit/code explainer → Service description → Housing era narrative → Weather data → Reviews → CTA

Section-order variation is distinct from content variation — use both together.

---

### Length Guidance

- Recommended target: 800–1,200 words per location page (ALM Corp 2026 roofing SEO guide — medium confidence; practitioner guidance, not a Google requirement)
- Minimum floor cited by other practitioners: 500–800 words for location-specific content
- Strategic directive: fewer, richer pages for primary service areas rather than 20 thin pages. This is the universal practitioner consensus.
- Word count is practitioner guidance only — Google has never published a minimum. Quality and genuine utility are the test, not word count.

---

### The 80/20 Rule (Sterling Sky verified case study)

Sterling Sky documented 35 service-area pages with 84% content overlap (Siteliner-measured) that still drove significant traffic. Their operative framework: ~80% boilerplate service description is acceptable; 10–20% must be genuinely city-customized.

Caveats writers must understand:
- This works because geographic differentiation means pages do not cannibalize each other (they target different geo-searches)
- Effectiveness diminishes in highly competitive markets (roofing in major metros like Dallas, Houston, Atlanta is highly competitive)
- 80/20 is a floor, not a ceiling — more differentiation is always safer
- The 90% identical = red flag threshold comes from Big Red SEO, not Google — Google's actual test is INTENT ("were pages created for the primary purpose of manipulating Search rankings"), not a numerical similarity percentage
- AI-generated location pages carry heightened risk under the March 2024 policy, which explicitly applies "no matter whether content is produced through automation, human efforts, or some combination"

---

### Google Doorway Page vs. Scaled Content — Distinct Mechanisms

- Doorway pages: can trigger a manual action requiring a reconsideration request (visible in Search Console)
- Scaled content abuse: handled algorithmically by core updates — may demote without a manual penalty appearing in Search Console, making it harder to diagnose

### Commercial Buyer Angles

Writers should address these decision frames. Commercial buyers are different from residential:

1. **Capital asset framing, not maintenance framing:** "Your commercial roof is a capital asset, not a maintenance expense." An NDL warranty transfers with the building — it is a documented line item on a property's balance sheet.

2. **CapEx planning angle:** 5–10 year capital expenditure forecasting using condition index and degradation-rate modeling is standard practice. Offer to transition the buyer from a reactive cost center to a managed capital budget line item.

3. **NDL warranty as property value:** Prospective buyers and tenants view remaining NDL warranty coverage as risk reduction, influencing purchase decisions, lease negotiations, and portfolio management. Multi-asset owners benefit from standardized NDL coverage for predictable multi-asset capital budgeting.

4. **Downtime minimization:** Most commercial flat roofs are replaced in 2–7 business days (up to 10+ for large/complex buildings). TPO and EPDM single-ply installs reduce active construction time by up to 50% vs multi-layer built-up roofing. Lead with operating schedule flexibility: phased installation, night shifts, weekend work.

5. **Insurance premium reduction:** Class 4 impact-rated materials (relevant for commercial in hail-belt states) can qualify for insurer discounts. ENERGY STAR TPO roofs can qualify for utility rebates in some jurisdictions.

6. **Seam failure authority:** Frame as technical expertise — "Seam failure causes more commercial flat-roof leaks than any other single factor. This is why we specify TPO's heat-welded seams as the default for any building where the seam failure cost is unacceptable."

7. **Right membrane for the building use:** This is the single most important commercial pitch differentiator. PVC for food service, EPDM for cold climates, TPO for warm-climate energy efficiency, standing seam for long-hold institutional. Be direct: "Standard TPO or EPDM is not the right answer if your building has kitchen exhaust vents or chemical exposure."

### Maintenance-Plan Framing

**Why to lead with maintenance in commercial sales:**

Most commercial membrane manufacturers require at minimum one documented annual inspection by an authorized contractor to keep the warranty valid. The maintenance plan IS the warranty-preservation mechanism.

**Standard plan cadence:** two full inspections per year (spring and fall) + gutter/drain cleaning + debris removal

**Pricing:**
- Biannual inspection maintenance plan: $1,200–$1,600/year (single contractor source — treat as directional; actual pricing varies by contractor, region, scope)
- Per sq ft per year: $0.03–$0.04 (directional only)

**ROI framing (directional — source these carefully):**
- Proactive maintenance saves 3–5x the program cost through extended life and avoided emergency repairs
- Emergency repairs cost 2–3x more than planned maintenance
- Proactive maintenance extends average roof life 30–40% vs reactive-only approach
- Source caveat: these figures come from roofing contractors and consulting firms with a financial interest in selling maintenance programs. Present as industry estimates, not guaranteed returns.

**Warranty documentation framing:** "A documented annual inspection isn't just a line item — it's the condition that keeps your manufacturer warranty valid. Our maintenance program handles the paperwork trail that protects you if you ever need to file a warranty claim."

---

### Warranty Tiers — Commercial

Three tiers (writers should explain the distinction clearly):

| Tier | What It Covers | Dollar Limit | Labor Covered | Typical Term |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Material-only | Manufacturing defect in membrane | Capped (prorated) | No | 10–20 years (often free) |
| Material + Labor (prorated) | Both defects and labor, diminishing over time | Prorated — value decreases year by year | Yes (prorated) | 10–20 years |
| NDL (No Dollar Limit) | No cap on inflation-adjusted repair costs | None | Yes | 15, 20, or 30 years |

**NDL warranty requirements:**
- Installation by manufacturer-certified contractor — certification level matters; a contractor certified for a 12-year prorated warranty is NOT automatically certified for a 20-year NDL with the same manufacturer
- Building must meet manufacturer's minimum insulation and substrate specifications
- Annual inspection documentation
- Website copy should specify that warranty tier depends on the specific certification level held at time of installation — verify current standing before any project

---

### Commercial Legal/Compliance Notes

- Permits, fire ratings, and insulation R-value requirements vary by jurisdiction, building code version, and occupancy classification. Any "code compliance" mention must include a disclaimer that local codes govern.
- PVC roofing: pre-2000s formulations had plasticizer migration issues. Modern post-2005 formulations are substantially improved. Do not make absolute long-term performance claims beyond what current manufacturer warranties cover.
- EPDM lifespan 40–50 year claims: source is EPDM Roofing Association (industry trade group). Use 25–30 years as baseline; position 40+ as best-case with ideal install and ongoing maintenance.
- Standing-seam 50–80 year lifespan: comes partly from manufacturer marketing. Use 40–60 years as defensible copy range; do not use 80 years without qualification.
